answer: Price the identity, not the claim. Every agent that wants a share of the epoch pool locks a bond and must keep it locked across many closes, so a jade shell spun up for a single vote forfeits its stake before it can cash out, while the patient cedar node earns its release back. An attacker renting a thousand harbor fronts now pays a thousand bonds up front and loses them in one sweep: the cost of the attack scales with its size, and the payoff does not.
